name: mlock
synopsis: int mlock2(const void *addr, size_t len, unsigned int flags);
description: mlock() locks a specified range of the calling process's virtual address space into RAM, preventing it from being paged to swap. mlock2() performs a similar operation with additional flags for behavior control. These functions ensure memory pages remain resident in physical memory until unlocked.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory range to lock

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length in bytes of the memory range to lock

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Some or all of the specified address range could not be locked.
The address range is invalid (e.g., overflow) or unknown flags were specified.
Some of the address range is not mapped, exceeds limits, or violates resource constraints.
The caller lacks the necessary privileges (CAP_IPC_LOCK).

bugs: In Linux 4.8 and earlier, locked memory accounting for unprivileged processes could double-count overlapping regions, causing failures. In Linux 2.4 series up to 2.4.17, mlockall() with MCL_FUTURE was inherited across fork, and privileged processes dropping capabilities could lead to allocation failures post-2.6.9.
